note: Attacker-controlled bytes from the libFuzzer testcase are passed directly into the HTTP request parser entry point.
The input is copied into a fixed-size buffer and then wrapped as the request buffer for parsing.
During header parsing, an If-Modified-Since header is recorded as a raw pointer/length pair when the header name matches.
After successful request parsing, the stored header value is re-parsed as an RFC time string.
The raw header value is passed to the time parser without copying or additional validation beyond the earlier header match.
The parser assumes a 30-byte RFC 1123-style string and begins fixed-offset reads from the attacker-controlled buffer.
The macro expands to a 32-bit load from the current pointer, so the parser performs an unbounded read if the header value is shorter than expected.
Later fixed-offset checks continue dereferencing the same attacker-controlled string, matching the reported global-buffer-overflow READ sink.
